Open QC from Home. Inspect stored segmentation, unit, leakage and plate-effect checks. Open its nested viewers for detailed inspection. Input data: Measured objects; Quality-control results. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Measure to QC: Review available checks and missing evidence.

Open Database Browser through Help search, then choose Lineage. Inspect recorded cell/nucleus/pathogen/organelle containment links; this is object containment, not time-series lineage inference. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Experiment Design from Home. Enter conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, then export the experimental layout before acquisition. Input data: Screen design and power estimates. Screen design and power estimates: Saved planning tables or figures based on explicitly chosen effect sizes, variability and sampling assumptions. Output data: Experimental layout. Experimental layout: Exported plate/condition/control/replicate map. Keep its plate and well identifiers consistent with the acquired data. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities.

Open QC from Home, then choose Layer Viewer. Inspect aligned image, label and point/ROI layers for the selected field. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Power / Design from Home. Estimate sampling needs from chosen effect sizes and variability; pilot measurements are optional evidence for assumptions. Input data: Screen design and power estimates; Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Screen design and power estimates. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design.

Open Run Compare from Home. Compare compatible saved settings, counts and hit lists without treating changed input data as a controlled model comparison. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Regression results and hits. Output data: Run/model comparison. Run/model comparison: Comparison tables and figures from compatible saved runs or masks; agreement is not ground-truth accuracy. Regression to Run Compare: Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings.

Open Database Browser through Help search, then choose Tabulate. Choose grouping variables and measurement columns, then inspect pivot tables and groupwise sample sizes. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Dose–Response from Home. Supply dose and response columns, controls and units before curve fitting; this route does not require sequencing. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Assay results; Figures and table exports. Assay results: Assay-specific result tables and figures in the configured destination, preserving well and condition identities. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities. Measure to Dose–Response: Join the measured response to explicit doses and controls.

Find Project Browser in the application's Help or tools menus. Locate projects and inspect their stage, last run, disk use and stale outputs. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run history and artifacts.

Open QC from Home, then choose Outliers. Review robust object/well outlier scores and the selected exclusion rule before carrying filtered data into analysis. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports.

Open Embeddings from Home. Encode object images with a chosen model and channel policy. Retain object identities and encoder provenance when supplying the features to downstream exploration. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops. Output data: Image embeddings. Image embeddings: Object-indexed encoder features, with channel policy and encoder provenance. The encoding API returns features; persistence is caller-dependent. Measure to Embeddings: Retain encoder and channel-policy provenance. Embeddings to Image UMAP: Supply the encoder feature table with matching object IDs; do not assume every GUI route automatically persists it.

Open QC from Home, then choose Control Charts. Compare designated controls across plates and inspect drift; the definition of a control comes from the experiment. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Training Runs. Compare saved training histories, metrics and settings from compatible model runs. Input data: Run history and artifacts. Output data: Run/model comparison.

Open Align & Stitch from Home. Inspect tile geometry, overlap and channel mapping, then save the mosaic with coordinate records. OPS also needs the original cycle/site identities. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Aligned mosaic and coordinates. Aligned mosaic and coordinates: Align & Stitch destination: composed image and the tile-coordinate/layout records needed to interpret it. Align & Stitch to OPS: Carry tile coordinates and original sequencing cycles into OPS; a flattened mosaic alone is insufficient.

Open Make Masks from Home. Curate image/mask pairs for segmentation training, or use FEATURES to assign images and masks and invoke measurement. Saving a mask does not train a classifier. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Curated training fields; Label masks. Curated training fields: Separate image and integer-mask files with matching field identities; preserve original images and labels. Make Masks to Cellpose Workbench: Use independently checked image/mask pairs. Make Masks to Measure: Use FEATURES to pair images and masks and write a measured project; standalone masks are not merged arrays. Make Masks to Plaque Assay: Use plaque masks with matching source images; cell masks are not automatically plaque labels.

Open Graph Builder from Home, then choose Plate Viewer. Aggregate the selected measurement by well and inspect plate patterns and controls. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Image UMAP from Home. Project measured features or supplied encoder features and inspect representative crops. A cluster is a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. Use the lasso and annotation controls to write reviewed selections to an annotation column in the matching measurement database. A geometric selection alone does not establish a biological phenotype. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Image embeddings. Output data: Projection and clusters; Training annotations. Projection and clusters: Image UMAP/PCA coordinate tables, selected clusters and figures for the loaded measurement data. Measure to Image UMAP: Choose feature columns and inspect representative crops. Embeddings to Image UMAP: Supply the encoder feature table with matching object IDs; do not assume every GUI route automatically persists it. Image UMAP to Gate Editor: Supply the matching coordinate/feature columns when defining a selection. Image UMAP to Classify: Write reviewed lasso selections to an annotation column in the matching object database, then select that column in Classify. Inspect crops and validate labels; embedding clusters are not ground truth.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Prediction Profiler. Inspect how a fitted model responds as an input feature changes; predictions do not establish causal effects. Input data: Fitted feature classifier. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Graph Builder from Home. Choose variables, groups and plotting settings from the loaded table, then export the figure with its analysis context. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports. Measure to Graph Builder: Choose explicit variables, groups and filters.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Investigate Hit. Link a regression hit to candidate objects and quantitative well-level evidence. This does not independently validate the hit. Input data: Regression results and hits; Object classification scores; Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Investigate Hit: Join compatible phenotype and object data for the chosen hit.

Open Gate Editor from Home. Define threshold or polygon gates on actual feature/coordinate columns, then apply the saved gate to compatible objects. Use Annotate to write the displayed gates to an annotation column; review the selected objects and choose binary or multiclass labels. Input data: Measured objects; Projection and clusters. Output data: Reusable gates; Training annotations. Image UMAP to Gate Editor: Supply the matching coordinate/feature columns when defining a selection. Gate Editor to Annotate: Apply compatible gates, then review candidate labels. Measure to Gate Editor: Use the actual measured feature definitions and units. Gate Editor to Classify: Write reviewed gate selections to an annotation column, then select that same column and object population in Classify. Keep validation objects separate from training labels.

Find Feature Dictionary in the application's Help or tools menus. Look up feature definitions and units before choosing measurement columns. Input data: Feature definitions. Feature definitions: The installed feature dictionary; definitions describe existing measurements and do not compute them. Output data: Feature definitions.

Open Graph Builder from Home, then choose Small Multiples. Compare groups in small-multiple plots with explicit shared or independent axes. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Figures and table exports.

Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Plaque Assay. Analyse plaque images or existing masks with the configured plaque model. This route need not pass through Measure; use the dedicated plaque example. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Assay results; Label masks. Make Masks to Plaque Assay: Use plaque masks with matching source images; cell masks are not automatically plaque labels.

Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Recruitment. Use compartment intensity measurements and matching host/pathogen identities to compute recruitment ratios. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Recruitment: Require the intended compartment intensities and identities.

Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Host–Pathogen Analysis. Measure whole vacuoles and host reference compartments, keeping uninfected host cells for the infection denominator. Select marker channels and control-calibrated ratio thresholds. Optionally count individually segmented parasites from explicit vacuole links or a measured count column. Review vacuole, host and well tables, joint marker states, replication distributions and unmatched parasite links; unknown measurements remain unknown. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Host–Pathogen Analysis: Keep uninfected cells in Measure. Supply whole-vacuole masks, host reference intensities and optional explicit parasite-to-vacuole links; host identity alone does not define a vacuole.

Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Invasion Assay. Use the required two-colour differential-staining measurements and stain-baseline controls to distinguish attachment from invasion. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Invasion Assay: Require two-colour stain measurements and appropriate baseline controls.

Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Replication Assay. Count parasites using explicit vacuole identity and compare condition distributions; host identity alone does not define a vacuole. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Assay results. Measure to Replication Assay: Require explicit parasite-to-vacuole identities.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Cellpose Workbench. Open Cellpose Workbench inside Make Masks and train from verified image/mask pairs. Evaluate on separate fields before selecting the checkpoint in Mask. Input data: Curated training fields. Output data: Segmentation checkpoint. Make Masks to Cellpose Workbench: Use independently checked image/mask pairs. Cellpose Workbench to Mask: Select the saved compatible checkpoint in Mask. Cellpose Workbench to Direct Cellpose mask generation: Pass the trained checkpoint as custom_model with the matching image channels and preprocessing.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Mask the whole folder. Apply the selected segmentation model to the open image folder through Make Masks; inspect saved labels before measuring them. Input data: Microscope images; Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Label masks.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Model Compare. Compare model masks on identical fields. Without independent reference labels, agreement does not measure segmentation accuracy. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks; Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Run/model comparison.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Model Zoo. Inspect model provenance and download/install compatible checkpoints or backends. A listed backend is not itself a checkpoint file. Input data: Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Segmentation checkpoint.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Curate. Correct labels and track assignments while retaining a record of the edits. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks; Linked time-series objects. Linked time-series objects: Tracked labels and frame/object associations from the time-series project, with frame interval and units. Output data: Label masks; Linked time-series objects.

Open Make Masks from Home, then choose Napari Bridge. Send the matching image/labels to napari and import the revised labels back with field identity preserved. Input data: Microscope images; Label masks. Output data: Label masks.

Open Import from Home, then choose Import Images. Review field identities, image channels and optional external masks before writing a separate project. Image-only imports still need segmentation before measurement. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Microscope images; Images and label masks; Label masks. Import Images to Mask: Use imported image planes and identities; image-only imports still need segmentation.

Open Map Barcodes from Home, then choose Barcode QC. Inspect mapping depth, coverage, collisions and positional effects before guide-count filtering. Input data: Guide counts per well. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Map Barcodes to Barcode QC: Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.

Open Image UMAP from Home, then choose Image Scatter. Plot selected measurement columns with object-crop inspection. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops. Output data: Projection and clusters; Figures and table exports.

Open Image UMAP from Home, then choose PCA. Inspect principal components and feature loadings for the selected measured objects. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: Projection and clusters; Figures and table exports.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Volcano Explorer. Open a saved regression result and inspect effect sizes, adjusted significance and individual hit records. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Volcano Explorer: Inspect saved effects and adjusted significance.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Hit List. Filter and rank saved hits with their effects, FDR and guide agreement. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Figures and table exports. Regression to Hit List: Inspect ranked hits and guide agreement.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Methods & Results. Draft methods/results text from recorded settings and results; review every claim before publication. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Regression results and hits. Output data: Shareable reports. Regression to Methods & Results: Review exported prose and every traced result.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Diagnostics. Inspect the diagnostic panels saved by the chosen regression run; distinguish missing diagnostics from passed assumptions. Input data: Regression results and hits. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Regression to Diagnostics: Open the diagnostics actually written by this run.

Open Measure from Home, then choose Illumination. Estimate and apply flat-field correction at configured stages. Keep corrected display values distinct from raw measurements and record the applied policy. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Microscope images.

Open Measure from Home, then choose AnnData Export. Export an AnnData .h5ad file with object metadata and measured features for downstream single-cell analysis. Input data: Measured objects. Output data: AnnData export. AnnData export: An exported .h5ad file containing measured features and object metadata. Measure to AnnData Export: Export compatible feature and metadata columns.

Open Measure from Home, then choose Motility Assay. Inspect track speed and infection-related measurements with an explicit frame interval and pixel calibration. Input data: Linked time-series objects; Measured objects. Output data: Assay results; Figures and table exports. Timelapse to Motility Assay: Supply frame interval and pixel calibration. Measure to Motility Assay: Combine measured objects with matching tracks.

Open Mask from Home, then choose Timelapse. Open Timelapse within Mask to segment and link objects across ordered frames; inspect links before downstream motility analysis. Input data: Microscope images. Output data: Images and label masks; Label masks; Linked time-series objects. Mask to Timelapse: Enable the nested time-series route before generating linked labels. Timelapse to Measure: Use the time-series project with stable frame/object identities. Timelapse to Motility Assay: Supply frame interval and pixel calibration.

Open Mask from Home, then choose OPS. Use sequencing-cycle images and phenotype alignment to decode barcodes per nucleus. Aggregate/join the decoded identities to compatible phenotype inputs before Regression; the OPS database is not a drop-in FASTQ count CSV. Input data: Microscope images; Aligned mosaic and coordinates. Output data: Optical barcode assignments. Align & Stitch to OPS: Carry tile coordinates and original sequencing cycles into OPS; a flattened mosaic alone is insufficient. OPS to Regression: Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Classifier Evaluation. Inspect held-out predictions, calibration and split/leakage evidence for the matching classifier. Input data: Classifier evaluation bundle. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Classify to Classifier Evaluation: Use the matching held-out predictions and split metadata.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Explain CV Model. Fit a measured-feature surrogate to existing computer-vision scores, preserving identity joins. A surrogate explanation is not causality. Input data: Measured objects; Object classification scores. Output data: Fitted feature classifier; Figures and table exports. Classify to Explain CV Model: Select CV predictions and the matching measured objects.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Activation. Apply the matching image classifier and preprocessing to inspect saliency/model-response maps. Input data: Trained image classifier; Object crops. Output data: Image attribution maps. Image attribution maps: Saved model-response/saliency images for the matching classifier and input preprocessing. Classify to Activation: Also provide the matching crops and channel preprocessing.

Open Annotate from Home, then choose Annotator Agreement. Compare independent annotation columns and inspect discordant objects; agreement is separate from classification accuracy. Input data: Training annotations; Object crops. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Annotate to Annotator Agreement: Choose independent annotation columns for the same objects.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Computer Vision. Train an image classifier from labelled object crops, archives or supported streamed crops. Match channels and preprocessing when applying its checkpoint. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops; Training annotations. Output data: Object classification scores; Trained image classifier; Classifier evaluation bundle.

Open Classify from Home, then choose Tabular Machine Learning. Train a feature-based classifier from measured objects and labels. Inspect missing-feature exclusions and grouped held-out performance before using scores. Input data: Measured objects; Training annotations. Output data: Object classification scores; Fitted feature classifier; Classifier evaluation bundle.

Open Regression from Home, then choose Parameter Sweep. Run explicitly selected regression settings and compare their diagnostics. Keep the input data and evaluation question fixed. Input data: Object classification scores; Guide counts per well. Output data: Run/model comparison; Regression results and hits.

Open Toxoplasma from Home. Open the organism guide from Home, inspect the compartment diagram, then select Plaque Assay, Recruitment, Invasion Assay or Replication Assay. The four Coming soon tiles describe proposals and cannot run. The guide itself does not analyse a project or produce a measurement table. Input data: Bundled organism reference. Bundled organism reference: Installed organism descriptions and SwissBioPics cell diagrams; no project input is required. Output data: Organism guide and assay selection. Organism guide and assay selection: GUI-only compartment highlights and navigation to available assays; no measurements or files are produced.

Open Plasmodium spp. from Home. Open the organism guide from Home to read the planned malaria imaging workflows and inspect the shared apicomplexan diagram. All eight assay tiles are Coming soon; none starts an analysis or produces a result. Input data: Bundled organism reference. Output data: Organism guide and assay selection.

Open Candida spp. from Home. Open the organism guide from Home to read the planned fungal imaging workflows and inspect the generic budding-yeast diagram. All eight assay tiles are Coming soon; none starts an analysis or produces a result. Input data: Bundled organism reference. Output data: Organism guide and assay selection.

Use Endodyogeny size proxy from Python through spacr.submodules.analyze_endodyogeny. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Read measured compartment areas, annotate conditions and bin area ** 1.5 into log2 size doublings. Defaults aggregate pathogen area per host cell, not per vacuole: multiple vacuoles in one cell are combined. This is an area-derived size proxy, not measured volume or a parasite count. Use Replication Assay with explicit vacuole identity for parasites-per-vacuole counts. Configure compartment, area filters, calibration, conditions and grouping before calling the API; saving is optional. Input data: Host-cell-aggregated compartment areas. Host-cell-aggregated compartment areas: Each src project root/measurements/measurements.db; tables defaults to cell, nucleus, pathogen and cytoplasm, with png_list added for merging. The compartment setting selects the area column; default pathogen_area is summed per host cell. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: cell, nucleus, pathogen, cytoplasm, png_list. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: cell_id, pathogen_area. Output data: Area-derived size-proxy results. Area-derived size-proxy results: Returned data and chi_squared DataFrames; save=True also writes data.csv, chi_squared_results.csv, chi_squared_pairwise_results.csv and a figure under the first project root/results/analyze_endodyogeny/. Relevant columns depend on the selected route: pathogen_area, pathogen_volume, pathogen_volume_bin, bin_index. Measure to Endodyogeny size proxy: Supply the measured project roots and required object/png_list tables. Verify host-cell aggregation and area units before interpreting size bins; the Mask counts database alone is insufficient.

Use Direct Cellpose mask generation from Python through spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Run a stock or custom Cellpose model on TIFF fields through the Python API. Despite its historical identify_masks_finetune name, this function performs inference, not training. Review normalization, channels, resizing and model parameters; masks are written only when save is enabled. Import compatible image/mask pairs through External Masks before Measure, or curate the pairs before training. This call does not build a Measure-ready merged project. Input data: TIFF fields for direct Cellpose inference; Segmentation checkpoint. TIFF fields for direct Cellpose inference: Top-level, lowercase .tif files in src; existing same-name files in src/masks are skipped. Supply the configured channels and a compatible stock model_name or custom_model checkpoint. Output data: Direct Cellpose TIFF masks. Direct Cellpose TIFF masks: When save=True, src/masks/<image-name>.tif contains integer labels. The call returns None and does not produce merged arrays or measurements.db. Cellpose Workbench to Direct Cellpose mask generation: Pass the trained checkpoint as custom_model with the matching image channels and preprocessing. Direct Cellpose mask generation to External Masks: Provide the saved label TIFFs and their original images to External Masks, assign object roles and create the merged project before Measure.

Use Pooled-screen simulation sweep from Python through spacr.sim.run_multiple_simulations. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Use the Python sweep API to explore stated screen-design assumptions. It expands combinations, runs simulations in a process pool and writes synthetic summary statistics; it returns None. Set a small explicit max_workers value and a bounded parameter grid before running. The output does not replace measurements or barcode counts for experimental Regression. Use the findings as planning evidence, with their assumptions recorded. Review the synthetic summaries when choosing planning assumptions; transfer those assumptions manually into Power / Design or Experiment Design. Neither tool imports this simulation database, and neither exports the simulation settings grid. Input data: Pooled-screen simulation assumptions. Pooled-screen simulation assumptions: Python settings dictionary: iterable sweep values for screen size, occupancy, classifier accuracy and sequencing assumptions, plus replicates, src, name, variable, plot and max_workers. generate_parameters expands their Cartesian product; begin with a small sweep and an explicit worker bound. Output data: Synthetic screen simulation summaries. Synthetic screen simulation summaries: src/<YYMMDD>/<name>/simulations.db; the sweep appends summary rows to simulations and optionally writes plots. These are synthetic performance estimates, not measured experimental hits. Relevant tables depend on the selected route: simulations.

Return to the chapter matching your next data product rather than repeating work you already completed. A count table is not a measured feature table, a projection is not a trained classifier, and a comparison is not a new experiment. The linked API pages carry the same file, table and column contracts, and the specialist lessons demonstrate the individual controls.

lessons.title: Image analysis modules and how they relate
lessons.description: Choose an image-analysis route through segmentation, measurement, annotation, classification, projections, gates, image registration, quality control and assays.
objectives: Choose a starting module from the data you already have.
Identify what each module reads and writes.
Follow the linked module lessons and API contracts for the next step.
lessons.prerequisite: Install spaCR and open Home. This lesson explains navigation and data handoffs; the linked module lessons provide the worked data examples. Inputs and outputs include conditional alternatives, as explained for each module.

scenes.narration: Begin on Home by deciding whether you have raw images, existing masks or measured objects. Mask creates segmentation outputs; Make Masks curates individual fields; Measure turns compatible images and labels into object measurements and optional crops. From there, the scientific question determines whether to classify, explore a projection, define a gate or run an assay. Align tiled images before the analysis that needs a common coordinate system. The routes here are alternatives and branches, not a requirement to run every module.

Open Embeddings from Home. Encode object images with a chosen model and channel policy. Retain object identities and encoder provenance when supplying the features to downstream exploration. Input data: Measured objects; Object crops. Output data: Image embeddings. Measure to Embeddings: Retain encoder and channel-policy provenance. Embeddings to Image UMAP: Supply the encoder feature table with matching object IDs; do not assume every GUI route automatically persists it.

Use Endodyogeny size proxy from Python through spacr.submodules.analyze_endodyogeny. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Read measured compartment areas, annotate conditions and bin area ** 1.5 into log2 size doublings. Defaults aggregate pathogen area per host cell, not per vacuole: multiple vacuoles in one cell are combined. This is an area-derived size proxy, not measured volume or a parasite count. Use Replication Assay with explicit vacuole identity for parasites-per-vacuole counts. Configure compartment, area filters, calibration, conditions and grouping before calling the API; saving is optional. Input data: Host-cell-aggregated compartment areas. Output data: Area-derived size-proxy results. Measure to Endodyogeny size proxy: Supply the measured project roots and required object/png_list tables. Verify host-cell aggregation and area units before interpreting size bins; the Mask counts database alone is insufficient.

Use Direct Cellpose mask generation from Python through spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Run a stock or custom Cellpose model on TIFF fields through the Python API. Despite its historical identify_masks_finetune name, this function performs inference, not training. Review normalization, channels, resizing and model parameters; masks are written only when save is enabled. Import compatible image/mask pairs through External Masks before Measure, or curate the pairs before training. This call does not build a Measure-ready merged project. Input data: TIFF fields for direct Cellpose inference; Segmentation checkpoint. Output data: Direct Cellpose TIFF masks.

For high-content analysis, follow Mask into Measure and then choose the method that answers your question. For segmentation training, curate image-mask pairs in Make Masks before Train Cellpose and test the saved model in Mask. Existing compatible masks or measurements let you enter later. Preserve channel identities, units, object keys and the settings used to create each result; follow the dedicated walkthrough for the route you choose.

lessons.title: 시퀀싱 모듈과 모듈 간 연결
lessons.description: 시퀀싱 및 광학 바코드 작업 흐름을 표현형 점수, 회귀, 실험 설계, 검정력 추정, 용량 반응 분석 및 실행 비교와 연결합니다.
objectives: 이미 보유한 데이터에 따라 시작 모듈을 선택합니다.
각 모듈이 읽고 쓰는 데이터를 파악합니다.
연결된 모듈 강의와 API 설명을 참고하여 다음 단계로 진행합니다.
lessons.prerequisite: spaCR을 설치하고 Home을 여세요. 이 강의는 화면 이동과 데이터 전달을 설명하며, 연결된 모듈 강의에서 데이터를 사용하는 실제 작업 예제를 제공합니다. 입력과 출력에는 조건에 따라 선택하는 대안이 있으며 각 모듈에서 설명합니다.

scenes.narration: Home에서 연구 질문과 바코드 데이터 유형을 먼저 확인합니다. Map Barcodes는 시퀀싱 파일을 읽고, 광학 풀링 스크리닝은 OPS를 통해 정합된 주기별 이미지를 읽습니다. 두 방식 모두 바코드 식별 정보와 실험 사이의 명시적인 대응 관계가 필요합니다. Regression은 호환되는 교란 계수와 표현형 점수를 연결하며, 바코드 해독을 대신하지 않습니다. 스크리닝을 계획할 때 Experiment Design과 Power는 데이터 수집 전에 사용하고, Dose-Response와 Run Compare는 수집 후 적합한 결과를 살펴보는 데 사용합니다.

Home에서 Map Barcodes를 엽니다. 실험 정보를 부호화하는 참조 데이터를 제공합니다. 웰별 가이드 계수를 표현형 점수와 짝짓기 전에 매핑된 계수와 바코드 품질 관리 결과를 확인합니다. 입력 데이터: 시퀀싱 리드. 출력 데이터: 웰별 가이드 계수. Map Barcodes에서 Regression으로: 일관된 플레이트 및 웰 키를 사용하여 가이드 계수를 표현형 점수와 짝짓습니다. Map Barcodes에서 Barcode QC로: 가이드를 필터링하기 전에 매핑과 커버리지를 확인합니다.

Home에서 Map Barcodes를 연 다음 Barcode QC를 선택합니다. 가이드 계수를 필터링하기 전에 매핑 깊이, 커버리지, 충돌 및 위치 효과를 살펴봅니다. 입력 데이터: 웰별 가이드 계수. 출력 데이터: 품질 관리 결과, 그림 및 표 내보내기. Map Barcodes에서 Barcode QC로: 가이드를 필터링하기 전에 매핑과 커버리지를 확인합니다.

Home에서 Mask를 연 다음 OPS를 선택합니다. 시퀀싱 주기별 이미지와 표현형 이미지 정렬을 사용하여 핵별 바코드를 해독합니다. Regression 전에 해독한 식별 정보를 집계하거나 호환되는 표현형 입력과 조인합니다. OPS 데이터베이스는 FASTQ 기반 계수 CSV를 그대로 대체하지 않습니다. 입력 데이터: 현미경 이미지, 정렬된 모자이크 및 좌표. 출력 데이터: 광학 바코드 할당. OPS에서 Regression으로: Regression 전에 해독한 객체를 표현형 및 가이드 입력과 명시적으로 조인하거나 집계합니다. CSV를 바로 전달하는 과정이 아닙니다.

Home에서 Regression을 엽니다. 표현형 입력과 가이드 계수 입력의 플레이트 및 웰 식별자를 일치시키고 반응 변수와 대조군을 선택한 뒤, 히트를 해석하기 전에 진단 결과를 살펴봅니다. 직접 측정한 반응도 지원합니다. 입력 데이터: 객체 분류 점수, 웰별 가이드 계수, 광학 바코드 할당, 측정된 객체. 출력 데이터: 회귀 결과 및 히트. Classify에서 Regression으로: 원하는 CV 또는 ML 점수 열을 선택하고 플레이트 및 웰 식별 정보를 유지합니다. Map Barcodes에서 Regression으로: 일관된 플레이트 및 웰 키를 사용하여 가이드 계수를 표현형 점수와 짝짓습니다. OPS에서 Regression으로: Regression 전에 해독한 객체를 표현형 및 가이드 입력과 명시적으로 조인하거나 집계합니다. CSV를 바로 전달하는 과정이 아닙니다. Regression에서 Run Compare로: 호환되는 저장된 결과 집합과 해당 설정을 비교합니다.

Home에서 Power / Design을 엽니다. 선택한 효과 크기와 변동성을 바탕으로 필요한 표본 규모를 추정합니다. 예비 실험 측정값은 필요에 따라 가정을 뒷받침하는 근거로 사용할 수 있습니다. 입력 데이터: 스크리닝 설계 및 검정력 추정, 측정된 객체, 실험 배치. 출력 데이터: 스크리닝 설계 및 검정력 추정. Experiment Design에서 Power / Design으로: 실험 배치를 사용하여 표본 추출 가정을 정한 다음 설계를 수정합니다.

Home에서 Experiment Design을 엽니다. 조건, 대조군, 반복 및 플레이트 제약을 입력한 다음 데이터 수집 전에 실험 배치를 내보냅니다. 입력 데이터: 스크리닝 설계 및 검정력 추정. 출력 데이터: 실험 배치. Experiment Design에서 Power / Design으로: 실험 배치를 사용하여 표본 추출 가정을 정한 다음 설계를 수정합니다. Experiment Design에서 Dose–Response로: 먼저 실험을 수행하고 측정하며, 용량 및 조건 식별 정보를 유지합니다.

Home에서 Dose–Response를 엽니다. 곡선 적합 전에 용량 및 반응 열, 대조군, 단위를 제공합니다. 이 경로에는 시퀀싱이 필요하지 않습니다. 입력 데이터: 측정된 객체, 실험 배치. 출력 데이터: 분석 결과, 그림 및 표 내보내기. Experiment Design에서 Dose–Response로: 먼저 실험을 수행하고 측정하며, 용량 및 조건 식별 정보를 유지합니다.

Home에서 Run Compare를 엽니다. 호환되는 저장된 설정, 계수 및 히트 목록을 비교합니다. 입력 데이터가 달라진 경우를 통제된 모델 비교로 취급하지 마세요. 입력 데이터: 실행 기록 및 산출물, 회귀 결과 및 히트. 출력 데이터: 실행 또는 모델 비교. Regression에서 Run Compare로: 호환되는 저장된 결과 집합과 해당 설정을 비교합니다.

Python에서 spacr.sim.run_multiple_simulations를 통해 풀링 스크리닝 시뮬레이션 매개변수 탐색을 사용합니다. 이 작업 흐름은 API 전용이며 Home 타일이나 메뉴 항목이 없습니다. Python 매개변수 탐색 API를 사용하여 명시한 스크리닝 설계 가정을 검토합니다. 매개변수 조합을 펼치고 프로세스 풀에서 시뮬레이션을 실행하여 합성 데이터의 요약 통계를 기록하며, None을 반환합니다. 실행 전에 max_workers를 명시적으로 작은 값으로 설정하고 매개변수 격자 범위를 제한하세요. 출력은 실험 데이터의 Regression에 필요한 측정값이나 바코드 계수를 대신하지 않습니다. 가정을 기록하고 결과를 계획의 근거로 사용합니다. 계획 가정을 선택할 때 합성 데이터 요약을 검토한 뒤, 해당 가정을 Power / Design 또는 Experiment Design에 수동으로 옮깁니다. 두 도구 모두 이 시뮬레이션 데이터베이스를 가져오지 않으며, 시뮬레이션 설정 격자를 내보내지도 않습니다. 입력 데이터: 풀링 스크리닝 시뮬레이션 가정. 출력 데이터: 합성 스크리닝 시뮬레이션 요약.

시퀀싱 참조 데이터와 플레이트 배치를 계수와 함께 보관하고, 회귀를 해석하기 전에 이미지 기반 점수와의 조인을 확인합니다. 광학 할당에는 별도의 객체 조인과 집계가 필요하며, 시퀀싱 계수 파일을 자동으로 그대로 대체할 수 없습니다. 계획 가정, 적합된 효과, 완료된 실행 간 비교를 서로 다른 결과로 구분합니다. 연결된 강의와 Home에서 시작하는 안내가 각 실험 유형의 경로를 보여 줍니다.

lessons.title: Toxoplasma: explore the page and choose an assay
lessons.description: Open the organism page, explore the cell diagram and choose an available assay.
objectives: Open the page from Home and find its main controls.
Identify the available inputs, actions and outputs.
Choose the next available analysis or reference.
lessons.prerequisite: Open spaCR Home. The organism guide requires no input files. Each assay has its own inputs and linked walkthrough.

scenes.narration: From Home, choose Toxoplasma. This page brings the organism guide, cell diagram and available assays together. You can explore it before loading any images or measurements.
Read the introduction in the information pane. Scroll each pane independently, or drag the divider to give the guide or assay tiles more room.
Hover over a cell component to read its description. Select several components to keep them highlighted, and use Clear components to reset the diagram.

Choose Plaque Assay for plaque counts and areas, Invasion Assay for entry measurements, Recruitment for marker ratios, Replication Assay for parasite counts, or Host–Pathogen for linked vacuole and host summaries. Open the matching lesson for its inputs, settings and results.
Click Host–Pathogen to open its analysis screen. Use Load test data to start with the supplied microscopy example, then follow the Host–Pathogen tutorial through the settings, preview and Run.

Return to Toxoplasma and choose Starplast to explore the knowledge map in its separate application. On first use, follow the offered installation steps. The reference links also open organism resources in your browser.
The guide itself writes no analysis files. Return to Home when you need image segmentation or measurement first; use the assay pages once the required images or tables are ready.

lessons.title: Plasmodium: explore the organism guide
lessons.description: Browse the Plasmodium guide, explore the cell diagram and find available general image-analysis workflows.
objectives: Open the page from Home and find its main controls.
Identify the available inputs, actions and outputs.
Choose the next available analysis or reference.
lessons.prerequisite: Open spaCR Home. No input files are needed for the guide. The Plasmodium-specific assay tiles currently show Coming soon.

scenes.narration: From Home, choose Plasmodium. Open this guide to browse organism information, cell compartments and the planned assay topics.
Scroll the information pane to read the blood-stage, liver-stage and motility sections. Drag the divider to adjust the space beside the module tiles.
Hover over the apicomplexan diagram for compartment descriptions. Select components to highlight them together, then use Clear components to reset the view.

The assay tiles currently show Coming soon and are disabled. Browse their descriptions to see the intended readouts. For an available image workflow, return to Home and open Mask or Measure with your own images and suitable channel settings.
Use the PlasmoDB and UniProt links to open organism resources in your browser. The guide requires no dataset, has no Run action and creates no output files.

lessons.title: Candida: explore the organism guide
lessons.description: Browse the Candida guide, explore the yeast diagram and find available general image-analysis workflows.
objectives: Open the page from Home and find its main controls.
Identify the available inputs, actions and outputs.
Choose the next available analysis or reference.
lessons.prerequisite: Open spaCR Home. No input files are needed for the guide. The Candida-specific assay tiles currently show Coming soon.

scenes.narration: From Home, choose Candida. Browse the guide for morphology, filamentation, biofilm and host-cell interaction topics.
Scroll the information pane and review the module descriptions beside it. Drag the divider to make either pane wider when reading.
Hover over a component in the budding-yeast diagram to read its description. Select several components to keep them highlighted, and use Clear components to reset the selection.

The Candida-specific assay tiles currently show Coming soon and are disabled. To analyse images with the available general tools, return to Home, select Mask and Measure, and choose channels and masks suited to your species and experiment.

Open the Candida Genome Database or UniProt links for gene and protein information. This guide uses no input files and writes no analysis outputs. Follow a runnable module’s tutorial when you are ready to process images.

lessons.title: Host–Pathogen: link vacuole markers and parasite counts
lessons.description: Load the microscopy example, choose marker and count inputs, inspect the preview, and export linked vacuole, host-cell and well summaries.
objectives: Load the example project and identify the host and vacuole measurements.
Choose marker channels and inspect vacuole-level recruitment in Live preview.
Run the analysis and read the output tables with the correct denominators.
lessons.prerequisite: Use Load test data for the supplied THP-1 microscopy example, or select a measured project with host cells, vacuoles and host-reference intensities. Retain uninfected host cells during Measure when you need an infection denominator. Individual parasite counts require a linked parasite table or a measured count column.

scenes.narration: From Home, open Toxoplasma, then choose Host–Pathogen. This module joins vacuole marker measurements and parasite counts to their host cells and well summaries.

Choose Load test data to download the microscopy example and fill in its settings. It contains two fields with images, host and vacuole masks, and measurement tables. Use it to practise the controls before selecting your own measured project.

Check Source. It should point to the project containing measurements/measurements.db. The module can also read a database directly or combine several project sources while keeping their identities separate.

Choose the vacuole table and its intensity-column prefix, then the host-reference table and prefix. The example uses pathogen for vacuoles and cytoplasm for the host reference. The object links must associate each vacuole with the correct host cell.

Set Marker channels to the zero-based intensity channels you want to compare. The example selects channel one for the RNF213 marker. Each selected channel needs intensity measurements in both the vacuole and reference compartments.

Leave Marker thresholds empty to inspect recruitment ratios first. To classify a marker as positive or negative, enter its channel number and a ratio threshold chosen from your assay controls. A ratio at or above the threshold is positive. Missing or invalid reference measurements remain unknown.

For parasite counts, choose either a parasite table with explicit parent-vacuole links or a measured count column on each vacuole. The microscopy example has neither, so keep both choices empty. Its parasite counts and replication readouts remain unknown.

Turn on Live, choose a field and click Run preview. Inspect the vacuole table beside the image. Select a row or click a vacuole to inspect the corresponding marker measurements and any available parasite count.

Turn off Live and expand Actions if it is folded. Keep Save enabled, then press Run. Wait for the output path in the console. Results are written to results/host_pathogen in the first selected project.

Open vacuoles.csv for one row per vacuole, including its host link, marker ratios, marker state and available parasite count. Open cells.csv for host-cell infection and vacuole counts, then wells.csv for their well summaries.

Use marker_states.csv to inspect joint marker states and replication_distribution.csv for parasite counts per counted vacuole. orphan_parasites.csv lists parasites without a usable parent link. Keep settings.json with these tables so the channel and threshold choices remain available.

Check the denominators before comparing conditions. Infection fractions use retained measured host cells, including uninfected hosts only when Measure retained them. Count distributions use vacuoles with known parasite counts; unknown values remain distinct from zero.
